claim: SGLT2 inhibitors are anti-hyperglycemic agents that prevent glucose reabsorption in proximal tubular cells.
source: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are anti-hyperglycemic agents that prevent glucose reabsorption in proximal tubular cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of action of SGLT2 inhibitors.

claim: SGLT2i improves renal outcomes in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients.
source: SGLT2i improves renal outcomes in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients, indicating it may have beneficial effects beyond glycemic control.
evidence: This statement references clinical findings but does not provide specific citations in this sentence, though it is supported by the broader literature context.

claim: SGLT2 protein is expressed in human and mouse podocytes to a similar extent as in tubular cells.
source: In vitro, we found that the SGLT2 protein was expressed in human and mouse podocytes to a similar extent in tubular cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B, C, and D.

claim: Immortalized podocytes from Col4a3 knockout mice accumulate lipid droplets.
source: Newly established immortalized podocytes from Col4a3 knockout mice (AS podocytes) accumulate lipid droplets along with increased apoptosis when compared to wild-type podocytes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: AS podocytes show increased apoptosis compared to wild-type podocytes.
source: Newly established immortalized podocytes from Col4a3 knockout mice (AS podocytes) accumulate lipid droplets along with increased apoptosis when compared to wild-type podocytes.
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Treatment with empagliflozin reduces lipid droplet accumulation in AS podocytes.
source: Treatment with SGLT2i empagliflozin reduces lipid droplet accumulation and apoptosis in AS podocytes.
evidence: This is supported by Nile red staining data shown in Figure 2F and 2H.

claim: Treatment with empagliflozin reduces apoptosis in AS podocytes.
source: Treatment with SGLT2i empagliflozin reduces lipid droplet accumulation and apoptosis in AS podocytes.
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Empagliflozin inhibits the utilization of glucose/pyruvate as a metabolic substrate in AS podocytes.
source: Empagliflozin inhibits the utilization of glucose/pyruvate as a metabolic substrate in AS podocytes but not in AS tubular cells.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3B and PDH activity data in Figure 3C.

claim: Empagliflozin does not inhibit the utilization of glucose/pyruvate as a metabolic substrate in AS tubular cells.
source: Empagliflozin inhibits the utilization of glucose/pyruvate as a metabolic substrate in AS podocytes but not in AS tubular cells.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Empagliflozin reduces albuminuria in AS mice.
source: In vivo, we demonstrate that empagliflozin reduces albuminuria and prolongs the survival of AS mice.
evidence: This is supported by albumin-to-creatinine ratio data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Empagliflozin prolongs the survival of AS mice.
source: In vivo, we demonstrate that empagliflozin reduces albuminuria and prolongs the survival of AS mice.
evidence: This is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show decreased serum blood urea nitrogen levels compared to untreated AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show decreased serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels in association with reduced triglyceride and cholesterol ester content in kidney cortices when compared to AS mice.
evidence: This is supported by BUN measurement data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show decreased serum creatinine levels compared to untreated AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show decreased serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels in association with reduced triglyceride and cholesterol ester content in kidney cortices when compared to AS mice.
evidence: This is supported by creatinine measurement data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show reduced triglyceride content in kidney cortices compared to untreated AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show decreased serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels in association with reduced triglyceride and cholesterol ester content in kidney cortices when compared to AS mice.
evidence: This is supported by triglyceride measurement data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show reduced cholesterol ester content in kidney cortices compared to untreated AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin-treated AS mice show decreased serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels in association with reduced triglyceride and cholesterol ester content in kidney cortices when compared to AS mice.
evidence: This is supported by cholesterol ester measurement data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Lipid accumulation in kidney cortices correlates with a decline in renal function.
source: Lipid accumulation in kidney cortices correlates with a decline in renal function.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analyses shown in Figure 7E-J.

claim: Empagliflozin reduces podocyte lipotoxicity in experimental AS in association with an energy substrate switch from glucose to fatty acids in podocytes.
source: In summary, empagliflozin reduces podocyte lipotoxicity and improves kidney function in experimental AS in association with the energy substrates switch from glucose to fatty acids in podocytes.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple experimental findings including respirometry (Figure 3), lipid droplet accumulation (Figure 2), and in vivo outcomes (Figures 5-7).

claim: AS is a hereditary disease of glomerular basement membranes caused by mutations in collagen type IV genes A3, A4, and A5.
source: AS is a hereditary disease of glomerular basement membranes caused by mutations in collagen type IV genes A3, A4, and A5 (Barker et al., 1990; Gross et al., 2016; Longo et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: AS is characterized by renal fibrosis with progression to end-stage renal disease in young adult life.
source: AS is characterized by renal fibrosis with progression to end-stage renal disease in young adult life (Barker et al., 1990; Grünfeld, 2000; Williamson, 1961).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Early treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors was shown to reduce proteinuria and delay disease progression in AS in both retrospective and prospective studies.
source: Though early treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) was shown to reduce proteinuria and delay disease progression in both retrospective (Gross et al., 2012) and prospective (Boeckhaus et al., 2022) studies, there is no specific treatment to prevent renal failure in patients with AS.
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: There is no specific treatment to prevent renal failure in patients with AS.
source: Though early treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) was shown to reduce proteinuria and delay disease progression in both retrospective (Gross et al., 2012) and prospective (Boeckhaus et al., 2022) studies, there is no specific treatment to prevent renal failure in patients with AS.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of treatment options, supported by the context of the literature.

claim: SGLT2i were recently found to protect from kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients with chronic kidney disease.
source: SGLT2i, initially developed for the treatment of patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), were recently found to protect from kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) (Heerspink et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a clinical trial.

claim: SGLT2 is most abundantly expressed in the apical brush border membrane of the proximal tubule.
source: SGLT2 is most abundantly expressed in the apical brush border membrane of the proximal tubule, where it plays a key role in renal glucose reabsorption (Vallon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: SGLT2 plays a key role in renal glucose reabsorption.
source: SGLT2 is most abundantly expressed in the apical brush border membrane of the proximal tubule, where it plays a key role in renal glucose reabsorption (Vallon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: SGLT2i selectively blocks SGLT2, thereby enhancing urinary glucose excretion and reducing glycemia.
source: SGLT2i selectively blocks SGLT2, thereby enhancing urinary glucose excretion and reducing glycemia (DeFronzo et al., 2017; Novikov and Vallon, 2016; Vallon and Thomson, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The major mechanism for renoprotection by SGLT2i is thought to involve the tubuloglomerular feedback and glomerular hemodynamics.
source: While the major mechanism for renoprotection is thought to involve the tubuloglomerular feedback and glomerular hemodynamics (Cherney et al., 2014), SGLT2i may also modulate key metabolic pathways linked to CKD progression.
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: In response to increased glycosuria, the body engenders a metabolic adaption to enhance the usage of fat for energy production.
source: In response to increased glycosuria, the body engenders a metabolic adaption to enhance the usage of fat for energy production (Ferrannini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: SGLT2i enhances β-oxidation in the liver.
source: Additional studies have also shown that SGLT2i enhances β-oxidation in the liver (Wallenius et al., 2022) and improves liver fat deposition in patients with T2D and fatty liver disease (Kuchay et al., 2018; Shibuya et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: SGLT2i improves liver fat deposition in patients with T2D and fatty liver disease.
source: Additional studies have also shown that SGLT2i enhances β-oxidation in the liver (Wallenius et al., 2022) and improves liver fat deposition in patients with T2D and fatty liver disease (Kuchay et al., 2018; Shibuya et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: SGLT2i lowers the cardiac content of cardiotoxic lipids in obese diabetic rats.
source: Similarly, SGLT2i lowers the cardiac content of cardiotoxic lipids in obese diabetic rats (Aragón-Herrera et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: The accumulation of both cholesterol esters and fatty acids in podocytes and tubular cells contributes to the pathogenesis of AS.
source: We and others have demonstrated that the accumulation of both cholesterol esters and fatty acids in podocytes and tubular cells contributes to the pathogenesis of AS (Ding et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2021; Mitrofanova et al., 2018; Wright et al., 2021), indicating that reducing the lipid content in the kidney may potentially reduce lipotoxicity-mediated renal injury in AS.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors and others.

claim: Reducing the lipid content in the kidney may potentially reduce lipotoxicity-mediated renal injury in AS.
source: We and others have demonstrated that the accumulation of both cholesterol esters and fatty acids in podocytes and tubular cells contributes to the pathogenesis of AS (Ding et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2021; Mitrofanova et al., 2018; Wright et al., 2021), indicating that reducing the lipid content in the kidney may potentially reduce lipotoxicity-mediated renal injury in AS.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited studies showing lipid accumulation contributes to AS pathogenesis.

claim: The metabolic substrates for ATP production are cell type-dependent in the kidney.
source: Although all cells in the kidney are high energy-demanding, the metabolic substrates for ATP production are cell type-dependent (Console et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: Renal proximal tubular cells use free fatty acids as the preferred fuel.
source: Renal proximal tubular cells in particular use free fatty acids as the preferred fuel, whereas inhibition of fatty acid oxidation (FAO) renders tubular cells susceptible to cell death and lipid accumulation (Kang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: Inhibition of fatty acid oxidation renders tubular cells susceptible to cell death and lipid accumulation.
source: Renal proximal tubular cells in particular use free fatty acids as the preferred fuel, whereas inhibition of fatty acid oxidation (FAO) renders tubular cells susceptible to cell death and lipid accumulation (Kang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature.

claim: Podocytes usually rely on glucose for energy production, while fatty acids are used as an alternative substrate.
source: Podocytes usually rely on glucose for energy production, while fatty acids are used as an alternative substrate (Abe et al., 2010; Brinkkoetter et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature.

claim: SGLT2 expression in podocytes was modulated by exposure to albumin.
source: Interestingly, a recent study demonstrated SGLT2 expression in podocytes and its expression was modulated by exposure to albumin, although the functional relevance of SGLT2 expression in podocytes is unknown (Cassis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The functional relevance of SGLT2 expression in podocytes is unknown.
source: Interestingly, a recent study demonstrated SGLT2 expression in podocytes and its expression was modulated by exposure to albumin, although the functional relevance of SGLT2 expression in podocytes is unknown (Cassis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: SGLT2 is expressed in both glomerular and proximal tubule regions of normal human kidney.
source: Immunohistochemistry in normal human kidney sections demonstrated both glomerular and proximal tubule expression of SGLT2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SGLT2 protein expression levels in cultured human podocytes are similar to those in HK2 tubular cells.
source: Using western blot analysis, we demonstrate similar levels of SGLT2 protein expression levels in cultured human podocytes when compared to HK2 tubular cells.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mouse liver lysate, HepG2 liver cancer cells, and kidney lysate from Sglt2-/- mouse do not express SGLT2.
source: Mouse liver lysate, HepG2 liver cancer cells, and kidney lysate from Sglt2-/- mouse were used as the negative controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B where these samples show no SGLT2 band.

claim: SGLT2 protein expression levels are similar in both tubular cells and podocytes from WT and AS mice.
source: We found similar SGLT2 protein expression levels in both tubular cells and podocytes (Figure 1C and D), while Sglt2 mRNA expression levels were significantly higher in AS tubular cells and podocytes than in WT controls (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Sglt2 mRNA expression levels are significantly higher in AS tubular cells and podocytes than in WT controls.
source: We found similar SGLT2 protein expression levels in both tubular cells and podocytes (Figure 1C and D), while Sglt2 mRNA expression levels were significantly higher in AS tubular cells and podocytes than in WT controls (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: SGLT2 is expressed in podocytes in vivo in Alport mice.
source: To confirm glomerular expression of SGLT2 in vivo, kidney cortices of Alport mice were co-stained with SYNPO and SGLT2 antibodies. As expected, the colocalization of SYNPO with SGLT2 staining confirmed that SGLT2 is expressed in podocytes (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Sglt2 is expressed in podocytes in the Healthy Mouse Dataset, though its expression level in every cell type is low.
source: In the Healthy Mouse Dataset (Wu et al., 2019), Sglt2 is expressed in podocytes, though its expression level in every cell type is low (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: AS podocytes are characterized by increased apoptosis when compared to WT podocytes.
source: We previously described that AS podocytes are characterized by increased apoptosis and lipid droplet (LD) accumulation when compared to WT podocytes (Kim et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: AS podocytes are characterized by lipid droplet accumulation when compared to WT podocytes.
source: We previously described that AS podocytes are characterized by increased apoptosis and lipid droplet (LD) accumulation when compared to WT podocytes (Kim et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: SGLT2i significantly decreases cytotoxicity in empagliflozin-treated compared with vehicle-treated AS tubular cells.
source: SGLT2i significantly decreases cytotoxicity in empagliflozin-treated compared with vehicle-treated AS tubular cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: No differences in apoptosis were observed in AS tubular cells treated with empagliflozin compared to vehicle.
source: No differences in apoptosis and lipid droplet accumulation were observed in any of the groups (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: No differences in lipid droplet accumulation were observed in AS tubular cells treated with empagliflozin compared to vehicle.
source: No differences in apoptosis and lipid droplet accumulation were observed in any of the groups (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: This is supported by lipid droplet quantification data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: AS podocytes showed increased cytotoxicity when compared to WT podocytes.
source: As expected, AS podocytes showed increased cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and intracellular LD when compared to WT podocytes (Figure 2C, D and F).
evidence: This is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: AS podocytes showed increased intracellular lipid droplets when compared to WT podocytes.
source: As expected, AS podocytes showed increased cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and intracellular LD when compared to WT podocytes (Figure 2C, D and F).
evidence: This is supported by lipid droplet quantification data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Empagliflozin treatment significantly reduced apoptosis in AS podocytes.
source: Empagliflozin treatment significantly reduced apoptosis and intracellular LD, but not cytotoxicity in AS podocytes (Figure 2C, D and F).
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Empagliflozin treatment significantly reduced intracellular lipid droplets in AS podocytes.
source: Empagliflozin treatment significantly reduced apoptosis and intracellular LD, but not cytotoxicity in AS podocytes (Figure 2C, D and F).
evidence: This is supported by lipid droplet quantification data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Empagliflozin treatment did not reduce cytotoxicity in AS podocytes.
source: Empagliflozin treatment significantly reduced apoptosis and intracellular LD, but not cytotoxicity in AS podocytes (Figure 2C, D and F).
evidence: This is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There is a positive correlation between lipid droplet accumulation and apoptosis in podocytes.
source: Interestingly, we observed a positive correlation between LD accumulation and apoptosis (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Treatment with empagliflozin significantly reduced the glucose content in both podocytes and tubular cells established from AS mice.
source: Treatment with empagliflozin significantly reduced the glucose content in both podocytes and tubular cells established from AS mice, which may result in glucose deprivation and a shift in energy fuel (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by glucose measurement data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Endogenous respiration measured in intact cells was not altered in AS tubular cells compared to WT.
source: Endogenous respiration measured in intact cells was not altered in either AS tubular cells or podocytes compared to WT (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Endogenous respiration measured in intact cells was not altered in AS podocytes compared to WT.
source: Endogenous respiration measured in intact cells was not altered in either AS tubular cells or podocytes compared to WT (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No difference in oxygen consumption rate was detected between WT and AS tubular cells in response to fatty acids.
source: No difference in oxygen consumption rate (OCR) was detected between WT and AS tubular cells in response to fatty acids.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: AS tubular cells show elevated respiration after the addition of NADH-linked substrates.
source: However, AS tubular cells show elevated respiration after the addition of NADH-linked substrates.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Treatment of empagliflozin did not affect the respiration of AS tubular cells independently of the substrate.
source: Treatment of empagliflozin did not affect the respiration of AS tubular cells independently of the substrate (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: AS podocytes showed a slightly but significant increase in FAO-linked OCR compared to WT podocytes.
source: In contrast to tubular cells, AS podocytes showed a slightly but significant increase in FAO-linked OCR compared to WT podocytes, which could be due to the increase in intracellular lipid accumulation.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The increase in FAO-linked OCR in AS podocytes could be due to the increase in intracellular lipid accumulation.
source: In contrast to tubular cells, AS podocytes showed a slightly but significant increase in FAO-linked OCR compared to WT podocytes, which could be due to the increase in intracellular lipid accumulation.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed increase in FAO-linked OCR.

claim: The addition of NADH-linked substrates to WT and AS podocytes increased OCR to approximately double the value recorded in the presence of FAO-linked substrates.
source: Moreover, the addition of NADH-linked substrates to WT and AS podocytes increased OCR to approximately the double of the value recorded in the presence of FAO-linked substrates, in agreement with podocytes preferential use of glucose oxidation for ATP production.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NADH-linked respiration in AS podocytes was inhibited by treatment with empagliflozin.
source: Interestingly, NADH-linked respiration in AS podocytes was inhibited by treatment with empagliflozin (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In podocytes established from AS mice, empagliflozin may induce a metabolic remodeling characterized by a reduction in glucose oxidation and a switch toward the use of alternative substrates for ATP production.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that in podocytes established from AS mice, empagliflozin may induce a metabolic remodeling characterized by a reduction in glucose oxidation and a switch toward the use of alternative substrates for ATP production.
evidence: This is an inference based on the respirometry data showing reduced NADH-linked respiration with empagliflozin treatment.

claim: PDH is an enzyme that converts glycolysis-derived pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and increases its influx into the tricarboxylic acid cycle.
source: PDH is an enzyme that converts glycolysis-derived pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and increases its influx into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: PDH plays a central role in the reciprocal regulation of glucose and lipid oxidation.
source: PDH plays a central role in the reciprocal regulation of glucose and lipid oxidation (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: PDH activity was reduced in AS podocytes by empagliflozin treatment.
source: We found that PDH activity was reduced in AS podocytes by empagliflozin treatment (Figure 3C), suggesting a switch to the consumption of fatty acids as energy fuel.
evidence: This is supported by PDH activity assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Reduced PDH activity in AS podocytes by empagliflozin treatment suggests a switch to the consumption of fatty acids as energy fuel.
source: We found that PDH activity was reduced in AS podocytes by empagliflozin treatment (Figure 3C), suggesting a switch to the consumption of fatty acids as energy fuel.
evidence: This is an inference based on the PDH activity data and the known role of PDH in glucose-lipid metabolism.

claim: Empagliflozin treatment reduced glycolysis in AS podocytes.
source: Additionally, we found that empagliflozin treatment reduced glycolysis in AS podocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by extracellular acidification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Aberrant glycolysis was inhibited by empagliflozin in diabetic kidneys.
source: This finding is similar to what was observed in diabetic kidneys (Li et al., 2020) where aberrant glycolysis was inhibited by empagliflozin.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: SGLT2 expression in mesangial cells and podocytes has been previously reported.
source: Though SGLT2 is typically expressed in proximal tubules, its expression in glomerular mesangial cells (Maki et al., 2019; Wakisaka et al., 2016) and podocytes (Cassis et al., 2018) has been previously reported, suggesting that these cells can be potential targets for SGLT2i.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Glomerular mesangial cells and podocytes can be potential targets for SGLT2i.
source: Though SGLT2 is typically expressed in proximal tubules, its expression in glomerular mesangial cells (Maki et al., 2019; Wakisaka et al., 2016) and podocytes (Cassis et al., 2018) has been previously reported, suggesting that these cells can be potential targets for SGLT2i.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reported expression of SGLT2 in these cell types.

claim: Empagliflozin shows a protective effect on the glomerular endothelium via podocyte-endothelial cell crosstalk despite the absence of SGLT2 expression in glomerular endothelial cells.
source: Despite the absence of SGLT2 expression in glomerular endothelial cells, empagliflozin shows a protective effect on the glomerular endothelium via podocyte-endothelial cell crosstalk (Locatelli et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: SGLT2 expression in mesangial cells is increased under high-glucose conditions.
source: SGLT2 expression in mesangial cells and podocytes is increased under high-glucose (Wakisaka et al., 2016) or protein-overload conditions (Cassis et al., 2018), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: SGLT2 expression in podocytes is increased under protein-overload conditions.
source: SGLT2 expression in mesangial cells and podocytes is increased under high-glucose (Wakisaka et al., 2016) or protein-overload conditions (Cassis et al., 2018), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Sglt2 siRNA transfection downregulates the expression of Sglt2 in AS podocytes.
source: We show that Sglt2 siRNA transfection downregulates the expression of Sglt2 in AS podocytes (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: siSglt2 AS podocytes showed reduced apoptosis compared with vehicle-treated siCtrl AS podocytes.
source: Similar to siCtrl + empagliflozin AS podocytes, siSglt2, and siSglt2 + empagliflozin AS podocytes showed reduced apoptosis compared with vehicle-treated siCtrl AS podocytes in the absence of changes in cytotoxicity (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: siSglt2 + empagliflozin AS podocytes showed reduced apoptosis compared with vehicle-treated siCtrl AS podocytes.
source: Similar to siCtrl + empagliflozin AS podocytes, siSglt2, and siSglt2 + empagliflozin AS podocytes showed reduced apoptosis compared with vehicle-treated siCtrl AS podocytes in the absence of changes in cytotoxicity (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CPT1A is the rate-limiting enzyme of FAO.
source: CPT1A is the rate-limiting enzyme of FAO (Schlaepfer and Joshi, 2020), which was found upregulated by empagliflozin treatment and knockdown of Sglt2.
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: CPT1A was found upregulated by empagliflozin treatment in AS podocytes.
source: CPT1A is the rate-limiting enzyme of FAO (Schlaepfer and Joshi, 2020), which was found upregulated by empagliflozin treatment and knockdown of Sglt2.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: CPT1A was found upregulated by knockdown of Sglt2 in AS podocytes.
source: CPT1A is the rate-limiting enzyme of FAO (Schlaepfer and Joshi, 2020), which was found upregulated by empagliflozin treatment and knockdown of Sglt2.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: Dapagliflozin treatment led to an adaptive preference of skeletal muscle metabolism for fatty acids, as evidenced by increased expression of CPT1A.
source: This observation is consistent with an interventional clinical trial in which dapagliflozin treatment led to an adaptive preference of skeletal muscle metabolism for fatty acids, as evidenced by increased expression of CPT1A (op den Kamp et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a clinical trial.

claim: Mice with experimental AS start developing proteinuria at 4 weeks of age.
source: Mice with experimental AS start developing proteinuria at 4 weeks of age, followed by death at 8–9 weeks of age.
evidence: This is a description of the natural history of the AS mouse model.

claim: Mice with experimental AS die at 8–9 weeks of age.
source: Mice with experimental AS start developing proteinuria at 4 weeks of age, followed by death at 8–9 weeks of age.
evidence: This is a description of the natural history of the AS mouse model.

claim: Empagliflozin extended the lifespan of AS mice by about 22% compared to untreated AS mice.
source: We found that empagliflozin extended the lifespan of AS mice by about 22% compared to untreated AS mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: No difference in blood glucose was observed in empagliflozin-treated compared to untreated AS mice at 8 weeks of age.
source: Blood glucose was measured at 8 weeks of age and no difference was observed in empagliflozin-treated compared to untreated AS mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by blood glucose measurement data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The ability of empagliflozin to prolong the survival of AS mice is independent of its anti-hyperglycemic effects.
source: These data suggest that the ability of empagliflozin to prolong the survival of AS mice is independent of its anti-hyperglycemic effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that blood glucose levels were not different between treated and untreated AS mice.

claim: Empagliflozin significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio in AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin, ramipril, and the empagliflozin + ramipril (E+R) combination significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and prevented body weight loss in AS mice (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by ACR measurement data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Ramipril significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio in AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin, ramipril, and the empagliflozin + ramipril (E+R) combination significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and prevented body weight loss in AS mice (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by ACR measurement data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The empagliflozin + ramipril combination significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio in AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin, ramipril, and the empagliflozin + ramipril (E+R) combination significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and prevented body weight loss in AS mice (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by ACR measurement data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Empagliflozin prevented body weight loss in AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin, ramipril, and the empagliflozin + ramipril (E+R) combination significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and prevented body weight loss in AS mice (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by body weight data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ramipril prevented body weight loss in AS mice.
source: Empagliflozin, ramipril, and the empagliflozin + ramipril (E+R) combination significantly reduced the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and prevented body weight loss in AS mice (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by body weight data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The empagliflozin + ramipril combination prevented body weight loss in AS mice.
